author: spec-agent
summary: Lift and shift of L1-accounts (14 live rules) from Python to Rust with parity. Behaviour is copied as-is, including the trailing-newline username quirk.

ADDED: minidon-rust: accounts (new Rust implementation of all requirements below)
delta.note: Python repository minidon is unchanged and is the read-only reference. No rule is modified or removed; L1-accounts/BR-001 to BR-014 are all live.

out_of_scope: fixing known weaknesses (follow-ups in human-decisions section 3 and 5)

ears.text: When a registration request is received, the system shall lower-case the username and accept it only if it consists of 1 to 30 letters, digits or underscores; otherwise it shall reject the request as invalid (422).

acceptance.given: no account exists with username alice
acceptance.when: a registration is submitted with username ALICE_01
acceptance.then: the account is created and stored with username alice_01

acceptance.when: a registration is submitted with an empty username, a 31-character username, or a username containing a hyphen
acceptance.then: the request is rejected with 422 Invalid

requirements.basis: README states the rule; the code lower-cases before matching (parity copy).

ears.text: When a registration request carries a username that is otherwise valid followed by exactly one trailing newline character, the system shall accept it and store it with the newline, exactly as the Python reference does, as a separate account from the same username without the newline (deliberate parity copy of a known defect).

acceptance.given: no account exists with username alice
acceptance.when: a registration is submitted with username "alice\n"
acceptance.then: the account is created (201) with the trailing newline retained

acceptance.when: a registration is submitted with username "alice\n"
acceptance.then: it is accepted as a distinct account and not rejected as taken (this is the look-alike behaviour, copied on purpose)

acceptance.when: a registration is submitted with username "alice\n\n" (two trailing newlines)
acceptance.then: the request is rejected with 422 Invalid

requirements.basis: Human decision 2026-11-13 (DEMO, kurtis): copy for parity. Rejecting such names is a post-cutover follow-up, out of scope. A parity test is required and the Rust code must carry an explicit note that the behaviour is deliberate.
requirements.note: Two-newline case: DERIVED from the Python pattern ^[a-z0-9_]{1,30}$ (only one final newline can match before end of input). Shown for the Rust regex design (OP-03). The regex engine must be able to express the optional single trailing newline.

ears.text: When a registration request is received, the system shall strip surrounding whitespace and lower-case the email, and reject the request as invalid (422) if the result does not contain an "@" character; no other email format check shall be applied.

acceptance.when: a registration is submitted with email "  Bob@Example.com "
acceptance.then: the email is stored as bob@example.com

acceptance.when: a registration is submitted with email "bob.example.com"
acceptance.then: the request is rejected with 422 Invalid

ears.text: When a registration request is received with a password shorter than 8 characters, the system shall reject it as invalid (422).

acceptance.when: a registration is submitted with a 7-character password
acceptance.then: the request is rejected with 422 Invalid

acceptance.when: a registration is submitted with an 8-character password

requirements.basis: Inferred from code. The 8-character minimum is a known weakness copied on purpose (raise to 12 is a follow-up, human-decisions section 3).
requirements.note: Length is counted in characters, not bytes; Rust must count characters (research risk: text handling).

ears.text: If a registration request carries a username that matches an existing account username case-insensitively, including a suspended account, then the system shall reject it with 409 Conflict.

acceptance.given: account alice exists and is not suspended
acceptance.when: a registration is submitted with username ALICE

acceptance.given: account alice exists and is suspended
acceptance.when: a registration is submitted with username alice

requirements.note: Interaction with REQ-002 is DERIVED: uniqueness compares the stored (lower-cased) string, so "alice\n" does not collide with "alice".

ears.text: If a registration request carries an email that is already registered on any account, regardless of suspension, then the system shall reject it with 409 Conflict.

acceptance.given: an account with email a@x.com exists, suspended or not
acceptance.when: a registration is submitted with email a@x.com

requirements.basis: Inferred from code, confirmed by test_emails_are_unique.

ears.text: When a registration succeeds on an instance with no accounts, the system shall assign the Admin role to the new account; for every later registration it shall assign the User role.

acceptance.when: the first valid registration succeeds
another valid registration succeeds

requirements.basis: Inferred from code (0.95), confirmed by test_the_first_account_runs_the_instance.
requirements.note: Admin seeding is a known weakness (instance takeover risk, OQ-001) copied on purpose; secure seeding is a follow-up.

ears.text: When the system stores or verifies a password, it shall use PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with 100,000 iterations and a random 16-byte salt, store the hash as "<salt hex>$<digest hex>", compare in constant time, and never store the plaintext.

acceptance.when: an account is registered
acceptance.then: the stored hash has the form 32 hex chars, a dollar sign, then 64 hex chars and no plaintext is stored

acceptance.given: an account was registered by the Python build
acceptance.when: the Rust build verifies the correct password against the stored hash

acceptance.given: an account was registered by the Rust build
acceptance.when: the Python build verifies the correct password

requirements.basis: Inferred from code. Hash format must be byte-compatible both ways (zero migrations, OP-05). Hash strength is a known weakness copied on purpose (OQ-003 follow-up).

ears.text: If a sign-in request carries an unknown username or a wrong password, then the system shall reject it with 401 Unauthorized and the same generic message (Invalid username or password) in both cases.

acceptance.when: sign-in with an unknown username
acceptance.then: 401 with message Invalid username or password

acceptance.when: sign-in with alice and a wrong password

requirements.note: Response timing and username discovery by other routes are known gaps carried to design (security lane), not fixed here.

ears.text: If a sign-in request is made for a suspended account, even with the correct password, then the system shall reject it with 403 Forbidden (This account is suspended).

acceptance.when: sign-in with alice and the correct password
acceptance.then: 403 Forbidden and no access token is issued

requirements.basis: README states the rule; enforcement is in Accounts sign-in. The 403 status is DERIVED from the code (Forbidden).

ears.text: When a sign-in succeeds, the system shall issue a random URL-safe access token that expires 30 days after issue (configurable through the token_ttl_days setting, default 30).

acceptance.when: sign-in succeeds
acceptance.then: an access token is returned whose expiry is issue time plus 30 days

acceptance.when: sign-in succeeds
acceptance.then: expiry is issue time plus 7 days

requirements.basis: Inferred from code and configuration default.

ears.text: When a request presents a token that is unknown, expired, or belongs to a now-suspended or missing account, the system shall treat the caller as signed out (no account); a protected route shall then answer 401 Unauthorized.

acceptance.given: a token whose expiry is at or before now
acceptance.when: GET /accounts/me with that token

acceptance.given: a valid token whose account is later suspended
acceptance.when: GET /accounts/me with that token
GET /accounts/me with no token

requirements.basis: Inferred from code. An expiry exactly equal to now counts as expired (<=).

ears.text: When a username lookup is made without an explicit request to include suspended accounts, the system shall treat a suspended account as not found (404 Account not found); the lookup used by registration and sign-in shall include suspended accounts. This lookup, get_by_username, is the stable identity API other capabilities call.

acceptance.when: GET /accounts/spammer
GET /accounts/alice

requirements.basis: Inferred from code, confirmed by test_suspending_through_a_report_hides_the_account. Stable API ownership is STATED in human-decisions section 3 (CF-004); its Rust shape is decided in the design ADR.

ears.text: If a profile update carries a display name longer than 30 characters or a bio longer than 500 characters, then the system shall reject it as invalid (422).

acceptance.when: PATCH /accounts/me with a 31-character display name
acceptance.then: 422 Invalid and the profile is unchanged

acceptance.when: PATCH /accounts/me with a 30-character display name and a 500-character bio

requirements.basis: Numeric limits are DERIVED from code constants. Counting is in characters (research risk: text handling).

ears.text: The system shall let an account hold an editable display name and bio, changed through PATCH /accounts/me.

acceptance.when: PATCH /accounts/me with a new display name and bio

requirements.basis: README states that profiles have a display name and a bio. The route is DERIVED from capability.md.

ears.text: The system shall let an account set a locked flag (default false) through PATCH /accounts/me and expose it on the profile; the flag shall be stored and returned exactly as Python does.

acceptance.when: the profile is read
PATCH /accounts/me sets locked to true

requirements.basis: Field and its purpose (locked accounts approve followers by hand) are STATED in README. The follow-approval mechanism is owned by L1-following and is out of scope here (DERIVED).

ears.text: The Rust Accounts build shall read and write the existing stored formats (enum names, date text, hash format) with zero schema migrations and shall not create or migrate the schema.

acceptance.given: a synthetic dataset generated by the Python app (OP-09)
acceptance.when: the Rust Accounts build runs against a copy
acceptance.then: all 14 rules behave as on Python and no schema change is made

requirements.basis: OP-05 decision (DEMO): Rust uses the schema Python already makes.

ears.text: Each of the 14 live Accounts rules shall have a parity test that passes against both the Python reference and the Rust build, with the same requests and normalised ids and timestamps.

acceptance.given: the parity harness with a fixed clock
acceptance.when: a rule's request is run against Python and Rust

requirements.basis: 14 of 14 rules (acceptance in the one-pager). Running each test against Python first is DERIVED (one-pager section 4); the harness design is OP-07 (read-only on the Python repo, includes non-ASCII cases).

ears.text: The Accounts routes shall return the same status codes and error body shapes, date format, and 404/405 bodies as the Python reference; the auto-generated documentation routes shall not be ported.

acceptance.when: each Accounts route is called with an invalid or unauthorised input
acceptance.then: the status code and body shape match the Python reference

requirements.basis: Contract decision OP-06 is a DEMO decision by kurtis (STATED there); applying it to the Accounts routes and the exact codes is DERIVED. Cases where Python returns a server error are carried to design, not specified here.

knownWeaknessesCopied: no sign-in throttling, username discovery, no body size limit, Python 500 cases (security lane, design inputs)
openItems: OP-03 regex engine must express REQ-002 (confirm in ADR)
OP-08 lane findings to be worked at design
DERIVED rules are treated as human-confirmed by the 2026-11-10 baseline sign-off (human-decisions section 4)
